title: Healthy Weight Check
tagline: BMI, waist-to-height ratio and a healthy weight range for your height
scope: For adults aged 18 to 99. It works out your body mass index (BMI), your waist-to-height ratio if you add your waist, and a healthy weight range for your height, using the NICE NG246 (2025) guidance. It is a guide, not a diagnosis. Your answers stay on this page: nothing is stored or sent.
q.eat: Do you have, or have you had, an eating disorder, or are you worried about your eating?
q.eatWhy: We ask because numbers about weight are not helpful for everyone. Your answer stays on this page.
q.waistWhy: Adding your waist gives a fuller picture of health risk.
q.bgWhy: Some backgrounds have higher health risks at a lower BMI, so the guidance uses lower thresholds for them.
q.mixed: Does your family background include any of the groups above?
q.loss: Have you lost weight in recent months without trying?

howWaist.title: How to measure your waist
howWaist.body: Stand up straight and breathe out normally. Find the point halfway between your lowest rib and the top of your hip bone, usually just above your belly button. Wrap a tape measure around your body at that level, keeping it level and snug but not tight, and read it without pulling your stomach in.
errors.age: Enter your age as a whole number of years, from 18 to 99.
errors.ageRange: This check is for ages 18 to 99. Please enter an age in that range.
errors.ht: Enter a height between 120 cm and 230 cm (3 ft 11 in to 7 ft 6 in).
errors.wt: Enter a weight between 25 kg and 300 kg (3 st 13 lb to 47 st 3 lb).
errors.waist: Enter a waist between 50 cm and 200 cm (19.7 in to 78.7 in), or leave it empty.
stops.under18.title: This check is for adults
stops.under18.body: BMI works differently for children and teenagers, who need age-based growth charts. Your doctor or school nurse can help you understand a healthy weight for your age.
stops.pregnancy.title: This check isn't suitable right now
stops.pregnancy.body: BMI and waist measures don't give a reliable picture during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Your midwife or doctor can advise you about weight at this time.
stops.eating.title: Thank you for telling us
stops.eating.body: Numbers like these aren't the most helpful thing to focus on, so we haven't shown any. Your doctor can help, and you can find free, confidential support near you at findahelpline.com.
weightLoss.title: Please see your doctor
weightLoss.body: Losing weight without trying can have many causes, and some need checking. Please make an appointment with your doctor soon.
thresholds.adjusted: Lower thresholds used for your family background.
thresholds.notSay: Standard thresholds used. For some family backgrounds the guidance uses lower thresholds, so a healthy weight may be lower for you.
range.title: A healthy weight range for your height
range.note: A guide for your height, not a target. Health is about more than one number.
waist.title: Your waist-to-height ratio
waist.meaning.healthy: Your waist is less than half your height, which the guidance describes as healthy.
waist.meaning.increased: Your waist is half your height or more. The guidance links this with increased health risks, such as type 2 diabetes and heart disease.
waist.meaning.high: Your waist is well over half your height. The guidance links this with high health risks, such as type 2 diabetes and heart disease.
waist.below: This is below the range the guidance describes. Your BMI result gives a better picture.
waist.needWaist: Add your waist above for a fuller picture: keeping your waist to less than half your height is a simple, useful aim.
waist.bmi35: At a BMI of 35 or more, your waist adds little to the picture, so the ratio isn't shown.
meaning.title: What this means
meaning.underweight: Your BMI is below the healthy range. Being underweight can affect your energy, bones and immunity. It's worth talking to your doctor, who can check for any cause and help you look after your health.
meaning.healthy: Your BMI is in the healthy range for your height. Eating well, staying active and sleeping well all help you stay well.
meaning.overweight: Your BMI is above the healthy range. Small, steady changes to eating, activity and sleep can make a real difference to health, and your doctor can help if you'd like support.
meaning.obese: Your BMI is in the obesity range. This raises the risk of conditions such as type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure and joint problems. Your doctor can talk to you about support that suits you.
meaning.eatingSupport: If you're worried about eating, weight or body image, your doctor can help, and you can find support near you at findahelpline.com.
meaning.class3: Your doctor can talk to you about support that suits you, including specialist services.
meaning.older: At 65 and over, BMI is a less reliable guide, and a slightly higher BMI may not carry the same risk. Keeping your muscle strength and staying active matter more than a number.
method.title: How this works and important limits
method.paras: ["BMI is your weight in kilograms divided by your height in metres squared. It is rounded to one decimal place, and your category follows the number you see.","Categories follow NICE guideline NG246 (2025): under 18.5 underweight, 18.5 to 24.9 healthy, 25 to 29.9 overweight, and 30 or more obesity. For people with a South Asian, Chinese, other Asian, Middle Eastern, Black African or African-Caribbean family background, the guidance uses lower thresholds: 23 to 27.4 overweight and 27.5 or more obesity, because health risks start at a lower BMI. The obesity classes are lowered by the same 2.5.","Waist-to-height ratio is your waist divided by your height, rounded to two decimal places: 0.40 to 0.49 healthy, 0.50 to 0.59 increased, 0.60 or more high. It is used when BMI is under 35.","Limits: BMI is a screening measure, not a diagnosis. It is less reliable for older adults, very muscular people, people who have had a limb removed, and during pregnancy. Measurements you enter yourself may not be exact.","Our other tools: the Daily Protein Target uses lower BMI thresholds only for Asian backgrounds, and the Diabetes Risk Check bands waist-to-height ratio slightly differently. This check follows the newer NICE NG246 guidance.","Sources: NICE NG246, Overweight and obesity management (2025), recommendations 1.9.7 to 1.9.15; Ashwell M, Gibson S, BMJ Open 2016;6:e010159."]
